outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, in a statement reported by UNIAN at 7:22 p.m. EET Thursday, Nov 19 (11:22 a.m. CT), said that on Friday, Nov 20, planned hourly power-outage schedules would be in effect around the clock in some regions. For all categories of consumers, Ukrenergo said the Friday schedules would range from 0.5 to 3 queues, corresponding to outages lasting from 2 to 12 hours, and that capacity-limitation schedules would apply to industry. Ukrenergo said the reason was the consequences of enemy attacks on the power system, and that energy workers were restoring damaged equipment and networks around the clock. No official national customer count was given in that Friday schedule notice. That official Friday schedule is later than Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning status update. Ukrenergo said that as of Thursday morning, Nov 19, consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Sumy regions remained without power after Russian attacks over the previous 24 hours on generation facilities and electricity transmission and distribution systems. UNN, in a 9:31 a.m. EET Thursday report (1:31 a.m. CT), and Ukrinform, in a 12:13 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:13 a.m. CT), both citing Ukrenergo, said energy workers were working around the clock to restore electricity. Ukrenergo said that because of damage to energy equipment, emergency outages were currently being implemented in the Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Ukrenergo said restrictions were being imposed in some regions through the end of the day: capacity-limitation schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules from 0.5 to 3 groups for all consumer categories. No official national customer count was given. UNN also cited Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi as saying that Russians attacked energy infrastructure, civilian enterprises, and residential buildings overnight, that destruction was recorded in 12 regions, and that electricity substations were attacked in the Zhytomyr, Chernihiv, and Mykolaiv regions. UNN quoted Koretskyi as saying residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, the Kharkiv region, the Cherkasy region, and the Donetsk region also came under attack, that eight people were wounded, and that one person was killed in the Chernihiv region; those casualty figures were not described as energy-sector casualties. Censor.NET, in a 12:50 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:50 a.m. CT) citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov at a briefing, likewise said consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Sumy regions had been left without electricity, and that emergency power outages were being implemented in the Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. It said a return to scheduled power cuts would be possible once the situation in the power grid stabilized, that most regions were also operating under hourly schedules ranging from half a shift to three shifts, and that power-restriction schedules were in effect for industrial facilities. It said a crew of power utility workers came under enemy attack twice in the Chernihiv region while performing their duties, with no casualties. RBC Ukraine, in an 11:04 a.m. EET Thursday report (3:04 a.m. CT) also citing Nekrasov, likewise listed those five regions as remaining without power as of the morning, but listed emergency outages only in the Kharkiv, Sumy, and Poltava regions; that shorter emergency-outage list differs from Ukrenergo's account and from Censor.NET's account of the same briefing, both of which also included Dnipropetrovsk. No official national customer count was given in those Thursday-morning reports. That Thursday-morning official status is later than Ukrenergo's Wednesday-evening notice that planned hourly power-outage schedules would be in effect around the clock on Thursday in parts of Ukraine. UNIAN, in a report updated at 9:44 p.m. EET Wednesday (1:44 p.m. CT) citing Ukrenergo, said that for all categories of consumers the Thursday schedules would range from 0.5 to 3 queues, corresponding to outages lasting from 2 to 12 hours, and that capacity-limitation schedules would apply to industry. UNN, in a 6:02 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:02 a.m. CT) also citing Ukrenergo, likewise said one queue means four hours without electricity, so Thursday's outages may last from two to 12 hours. Focus, in a 12:43 a.m. EET Thursday report (4:43 p.m. CT Wednesday) citing Ukrenergo, said the electricity-supply situation remained most difficult in the Kharkiv, Sumy, Dnipropetrovsk, and Poltava regions, that in Kyiv on Thursday power would be cut for consumers in all 60 subgroups, and that in Kyiv Oblast, stabilization outages would average about six hours a day. UNIAN, citing Sumyoblenergo, said that in Sumy region on Thursday the total duration of outages, depending on the queue, would be from 8 to 12 hours. Those Wednesday-evening schedule reports did not give an official national customer count. In his evening address on Wednesday, reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following a briefing from Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal, that the electricity-supply situation was then most severe in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions and also difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions, and that there had been strikes on Odesa and its surrounding region, as well as on the Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:13 p.m. EET Wednesday (5:13 a.m. CT), said Russia had carried out more than 1,000 strikes on energy facilities since September and that the attacks had caused new power outages in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, Rivne, and Cherkasy regions as of Wednesday morning; it said emergency power cuts were then being implemented in the Sumy, Kharkiv, and Poltava regions, and that Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo reported that by Tuesday evening it and Ukrenergo had once again restored electricity to 390,700 consumers. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa, Rivne, Donetsk, or Cherkasy; that is not an official restoration figure for earlier outages in those regions. Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne Regional Military Administration, said in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 8:50 a.m. EET Wednesday (12:50 a.m. CT) that a Wednesday morning Russian attack had left more than 80 settlements in the north of Rivne region without power; no later official customer count or restoration notice for that Rivne outage was found. In Russian-occupied parts of the Donetsk region, occupation authorities reported that forced outages were continuing on Thursday (see the separate occupied Donetsk region row). No official national customer count was found. A midday Thursday recheck at 12:05 PM CT Thursday found no later official national customer count and no later-than-morning official list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks. An evening Thursday recheck at 5:50 PM CT Thursday found no later official national customer count, no later-than-morning official list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks, and no early Friday, Nov 20, Ukrenergo morning status update; the latest official national guidance remained Ukrenergo's Friday, Nov 20, around-the-clock hourly outage schedules of 0.5 to 3 queues in some regions, as reported by UNIAN at 7:22 p.m. EET Thursday. A late Thursday recheck at 11:55 PM CT Thursday, after Friday morning had begun in Ukraine (about 7:55 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20), found no official Friday-morning Ukrenergo national status update listing regions with consumers still without power due to attacks, and no official national customer count. The latest official national guidance remained Ukrenergo's Friday, Nov 20, around-the-clock hourly outage schedules of 0.5 to 3 queues in some regions, as reported by UNIAN at 7:22 p.m. EET Thursday and also reported by RBC Ukraine at 7:08 p.m. EET Thursday (11:08 a.m. CT) and Apostrophe at 7:13 p.m. EET Thursday (11:13 a.m. CT).

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including new strikes on the morning of Nov 17 after earlier Nov 16 attacks on energy facilities in the region. Ukrenergo said consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power as of Thursday morning, Nov 19, and that emergency outages were being implemented there
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 9:31 a.m. EET Thursday, Nov 19 (1:31 a.m. CT) and by Ukrinform at 12:13 p.m. EET Thursday (4:13 a.m. CT), said that as of Thursday morning consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power after Russian attacks over the previous 24 hours, and that emergency outages were currently being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk, along with the Sumy, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions, because of damage to energy equipment. Censor.NET, in a 12:50 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:50 a.m. CT) citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the five regions with consumers left without electricity and among the regions under emergency outages. RBC Ukraine, in an 11:04 a.m. EET Thursday report (3:04 a.m. CT) also citing Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the regions remaining without power as of the morning, but did not include it in the emergency-outage list in that report. No official customer count for the region was given in those Thursday-morning reports. That Thursday-morning official status is later than Wednesday reports that emergency outages were not being applied in the region. D1, in a noon EET Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing energy companies, had said that as of Wednesday morning emergency outages were not being applied in Dnipropetrovsk region and that stabilization (scheduled hourly) outages were in effect throughout the day by Ukrenergo order; Dnepr.info likewise said emergency outages had been cancelled on Wednesday. Dnipro.tv, in a 9:55 p.m. EET Wednesday report (1:55 p.m. CT) citing DTEK, said stabilization-outage schedules would be in effect in Dnipropetrovsk region on Thursday, Nov 19, for all six consumer groups throughout the day; that Thursday schedule is not a new official customer count. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. This is a later, separate wave of outages from Monday evening, Nov 16, when DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in the region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. Zelenskyy, in the evening address reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), said the situation was also difficult in Dnipropetrovsk region; he did not give a customer count for the region. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found. A midday Thursday recheck at 12:05 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure. An evening Thursday recheck at 5:50 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure. A late Thursday recheck at 11:55 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure, and no official Friday-morning Ukrenergo status update superseding the Thursday-morning regional list.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. In a separate Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; that figure is for the southern Nov 17 attack and is not a later official remaining count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 19 statement, said that over the last three days its crews had restored electricity to 128,000 families in 192 villages and towns of the region after new Russian attacks, and that restoration was continuing but was significantly complicated by frequent air-raid alerts. The same statement's introduction said crews had restored electricity to almost 130,000 families who had been left completely or partially without power. That is a three-day restoration total for the region; it is not a remaining customer count and is not a confirmation of full restoration for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that earlier weekly total also does not give a later official remaining figure for this morning Nov 16 outage. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for this outage. A later Wednesday DTEK OEM item said crews would carry out urgent equipment repairs from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Thursday, Nov 19, with planned outages in parts of Izmail district and in Kyivskyi and Prymorskyi districts of Odesa and the suburbs; that is a planned Thursday repair outage and is not an official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Thursday-morning recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage; the Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this specific outage. A midday Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 12:05 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage; the Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this specific outage, and the Nov 19 three-day restoration total remained the latest DTEK regional restoration total. An evening Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 5:50 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage; the Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this specific outage, and the Nov 19 three-day restoration total remained the latest DTEK regional restoration total. A late Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 11:55 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage; the Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this specific outage, and the Nov 19 three-day restoration total remained the latest DTEK regional restoration total.

outages.cause: Russian attack on energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region
outages.affected: No official customer count. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 18 statement, said that toward evening on Nov 18 the enemy attacked energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region, and that outages were being recorded in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts. It said that as soon as it was safe, energy workers began inspecting equipment and clearing rubble, that the destruction was significant, and that repairs would take time. It did not give a customer count or a firm restoration time. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 7:04 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:04 a.m. CT) and by Interfax-Ukraine at 7:16 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:16 a.m. CT), said the strikes caused power-supply disruptions in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts, that no casualties had been reported, and that energy crews were assessing the damage and working to restore electricity. Suspilne, in a 6:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:16 a.m. CT) citing DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi's Facebook page, likewise said part of customers in those two districts were left without electricity and that restoring the damaged facilities would take time. This is a later, separate event from DTEK's overnight Nov 15 outage that left 41,000 customers without power, from the morning Nov 16 northern outage that left 52,200 households without power, and from the southern Nov 17 DTEK attack after which 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 19 statement, said that over the last three days its crews had restored electricity to 128,000 families in 192 villages and towns of the region after new Russian attacks, and that restoration was continuing but was significantly complicated by frequent air-raid alerts. That is a three-day restoration total for the region; it is not a customer count for this Wednesday-evening southern attack and is not a confirmation of full restoration for this outage. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for this outage. A Thursday-morning recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page found no later official customer count or restoration notice for this Wednesday-evening southern outage. A midday Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 12:05 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or restoration notice for this Wednesday-evening southern outage. Kyiv Post, in a Nov 19 report dated 12:26 p.m., said Russian forces damaged energy and industrial infrastructure in the southern Odesa region during a combined overnight attack into Thursday, Nov 19. It quoted Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper as saying that attack caused no casualties and did not disrupt electricity supplies, and that crews were working at the damaged sites. Kyiv Post said the latest strike followed another attack on energy facilities in the southern Odesa region that had caused electricity disruptions in parts of two districts. That Thursday overnight attack, which Kiper said did not disrupt electricity supplies, is a later, separate event from this Wednesday-evening southern outage and is not a restoration notice for it. An evening Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 5:50 PM CT Thursday found no later official customer count or restoration notice for this Wednesday-evening southern outage. A late Thursday recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page at 11:55 PM CT Thursday found no later official customer count or restoration notice for this Wednesday-evening southern outage.

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, Debaltseve, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Thursday, Nov 19, the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy said forced temporary outages were continuing because of emergency situations in the power system, damage to power networks as a result of UAV attacks, and a continuing shortage of available capacity and high load on operating equipment. Later Thursday afternoon, the same ministry said an emergency in the region's power system had partially de-energized Donetsk, Mariupol, and Makiivka, and had disrupted supply in Dokuchaievsk and in the Novoazovsk, Volodarske, and Volnovakha municipal districts
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. RIA Novosti, in a 5:52 p.m. Moscow time Thursday, Nov 19 report that was updated at 6:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday (8:52 a.m. and 9:16 a.m. CT), citing the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said an emergency had occurred in the region's power system, as a result of which Donetsk, Mariupol, and Makiivka were partially de-energized. The ministry also said electricity supply had been disrupted in Dokuchaievsk and in the Novoazovsk, Volodarske, and Volnovakha municipal districts, and that the exact list of affected settlements was being clarified. That Thursday-afternoon update did not give a customer count. Earlier Thursday, RIA Novosti, in a 1:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday report (4:16 a.m. CT) citing the press service of the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said forced temporary outages were continuing in a number of cities and municipal districts because of emergency situations in the power system, damage to power networks as a result of UAV attacks, and a continuing shortage of available capacity and high load on operating equipment. The ministry said the outages had affected 12 cities and municipalities of the region, including the Amvrosiivka municipal district, a significant part of whose territory remained without electricity. It said energy workers were continuing restoration work and that, as damage was repaired, the system stabilized, and technical possibility appeared, supply would be restored to consumers in stages. That earlier Thursday update also did not give a customer count and did not name all 12 cities and municipalities. News-donetsk.ru, in a 2:55 p.m. local Thursday, Nov 19 report (5:55 a.m. CT) citing Donetskenergo, a branch of JSC Yugo-Zapadnaya ESK, and the occupation Administration of the Donetsk urban district, said that because allowable network load had been exceeded, 102 transformer substations had been partially de-energized in the Budyonnovsky, Leninsky, and Proletarsky districts, and that 14,163 subscribers remained without electricity, with restoration work under way. That 14,163 figure is an official Donetsk-city subset for those three districts and is not a later official regional remaining customer count. The latest official regional remaining counts found remain those from Wednesday. News-donetsk.ru, in a 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing occupation government chairman Andrey Chertkov, said temporary outages were reintroduced Wednesday morning because of a shortage of available capacity and high load on the networks. It said partial outages affected Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Debaltseve, Yenakiieve, the Yasynuvata municipal district, Khartsyzk, Torez, the Shakhtarsk municipal district, and Horlivka, and that 125,000 residential subscribers remained without electricity and 228 boiler houses were de-energized. Later Wednesday, dnrnews.ru, in a 6:16 p.m. local Nov 18 report (9:16 a.m. CT) citing Chertkov, gave no new customer count; Chertkov said energy workers planned to reconnect all customers in the near future, which is not an official firm restoration time. Later Wednesday, RIA Novosti, in a 10:28 p.m. Moscow time Wednesday report (1:28 p.m. CT) citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin, said electricity supply had been restored for more than 500 transformer substations in five districts of Donetsk; those figures are substation restorations in Donetsk city, not a remaining customer count, and they do not replace the 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures. In a mid-afternoon Wednesday update, RIA Novosti, in a 5:20 p.m. Moscow time Wednesday report (8:20 a.m. CT) citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said 33,302 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk because 226 transformer substations had been partially de-energized in the Petrovsky, Kievsky, Kuibyshevsky, and Kirovsky districts; that 33,302 figure is a Donetsk-city remaining count, not a later official regional remaining count. Earlier Wednesday, news-donetsk.ru, in an 8:09 a.m. local report citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said 31,090 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk's Kalininsky, Proletarsky, and Voroshilovsky districts; that earlier city figure was superseded by later Wednesday updates. Earlier Tuesday, Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:31 p.m. local Nov 17 report citing the occupation energy ministry, said forced temporary outages were in effect in Donetsk, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Mariupol, Makiivka, Torez, Khartsyzk, and Dokuchaievsk, as well as the Yasynuvata, Shakhtarsk, Telmanove, Amvrosiivka, and Volodarske municipal districts, without a customer count in that evening update. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:30 p.m. local Nov 16 report, citing the occupation administration and Donetskenergo director Oleg Pavlyak, said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity, a figure later superseded by the Wednesday remaining counts. A midday Thursday recheck at 12:05 PM CT Thursday found no later official regional remaining customer count superseding the 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed. Marik.su, in a Nov 19 report timed at 4:58 p.m. and citing the television channel Mariupol 24, which cited the occupation administration of the Mariupol urban district, said that because of a shortage of generating capacity, temporary and emergency outages were continuing in Mariupol. outages.cause: Storms knocked down two major transmission towers and damaged a third at Wharminda on ElectraNet's 132 kV line between Cultana and Port Lincoln, cutting transmission supply south and west of Whyalla. ElectraNet executive network manager Alex Trento said Friday the towers were built to withstand a one-in-2,000-year weather event and that the localized weather appeared to have been even stronger than the winds they were designed for. In a later Friday-afternoon ABC News report, Trento said the towers that fell were designed to withstand up to around 170 km/h wind speed and were also tested to destruction to their design standard, that he did not know what the wind speed was when the towers toppled but that the probability of it occurring was "very rare," and that a structural fault in the towers was "a possibility" and ElectraNet was investigating. He said that, seeing the localisation of the event, ElectraNet still thought the towers had been designed and constructed effectively.
outages.affected: ABC News, in an article posted at 4:08 p.m. ACDT Friday, Nov 20, and updated at 4:27 p.m. ACDT Friday (11:57 p.m. CT Thursday, Nov 19), said that while a large portion of the region had had power restored, less than 2,000 properties remained without power as at 3:30 p.m. ACDT Friday (11:00 p.m. CT Thursday), according to SA Power Networks's outage map. That less-than-2,000-properties figure as of 3:30 p.m. Friday is the latest remaining count found. That later Friday-afternoon remaining count is later than earlier Friday figures in an ABC News live blog posted at 9:31 a.m. ACDT Friday and updated at 3:24 p.m. ACDT Friday (10:54 p.m. CT Thursday). The live blog, citing the SA Power Networks website, said that at 2:45 p.m. ACDT Friday (10:15 p.m. CT Thursday) the number of properties without power had dipped under 5,000 across South Australia, and that about 6,000 properties were still without power on the Eyre Peninsula and West Coast at 1:30 p.m. ACDT Friday (9:00 p.m. CT Thursday). Earlier Friday morning, the same live blog, citing the SA Power Networks website, said that as of 9:00 a.m. ACDT Friday (4:30 p.m. CT Thursday) there were about 10,000 properties without power across South Australia, down from a peak of around 30,000 Thursday evening, but the bulk of the 10,000 were on Eyre Peninsula, which has been islanded from the national energy market. ABC said about 24,000 properties on the peninsula were cut off on Thursday when the storm downed the towers. The Friday-afternoon article likewise said the storm cut power to about 24,000 properties at 3 p.m. on Thursday. ABC, citing ElectraNet, had said about 10,000 customers in Port Lincoln and surrounding towns had got their power back, and that ElectraNet reported that power was restored to the Port Lincoln area using local generators at 9:45 p.m. ACDT Thursday, Nov 19 (5:15 a.m. CT Thursday). InDaily, in a Friday morning Nov 20 report, likewise said that in a Friday-morning update ElectraNet said local generators restored power to about 10,000 customers in Port Lincoln and surrounding towns about 9:45 p.m. on Thursday. The Friday-afternoon ABC article said a 20-megawatt generator located in Port Lincoln had been powering the township and lower Eyre Peninsula since Thursday night, and that all residents in the area had been urged to turn off their solar panels so the generator would not exceed its level of demand. Premier Peter Malinauskas, as quoted in that article, said the generator was working as it should but that "we're not out of the woods yet," citing further storm events, extreme fire conditions over the weekend, and the risk that the aging Port Lincoln generator might fail. SA Power Networks, in an 8:30 a.m. Friday, Nov 20 update (4:00 p.m. CT Thursday) on its Eyre Peninsula outages page, said it was seeking the support of customers on Eyre Peninsula who had power restored overnight, that those customers were being supplied by temporary generation while ElectraNet continued to repair its network, and that customers with rooftop solar that exports to the network should switch off their inverters and leave them off until SA Power Networks advised them they could turn them back on. The South Australian Department for Energy and Mining said severe weather had caused significant damage to electricity transmission infrastructure, including the destruction of two transmission towers on the 132 kV line between Cultana and Port Lincoln, disrupting supply to communities across the central and lower Eyre Peninsula and West Coast. It said the Minister for Energy and Mining had declared an electricity supply emergency under the Emergency Management Act 2004, that the declaration took effect at 6:15 p.m. ACDT Thursday (1:45 a.m. CT), and that it will remain in force for 14 days unless revoked earlier. ABC, citing the Department for Education in South Australia, had said some schools had opened in Port Lincoln on Friday after power was restored to parts of the area, but that more than 30 sites remained closed as of 7:30 a.m. ACDT Friday (3:00 p.m. CT Thursday), including schools in Cleve, Lock, Penong, and Streaky Bay. Earlier Thursday figures, from an ABC News article posted at 5:59 p.m. ACDT Thursday, Nov 19, and updated at 10:33 p.m. ACDT Thursday (6:03 a.m. CT), said about 24,000 properties on the peninsula lost power after two major transmission towers were downed and a third was damaged at Wharminda, and that by 10:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday (5:30 a.m. CT) the number of properties without power had fallen to about 14,500. ABC said that as of 7:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday (2:30 a.m. CT), almost 29,000 properties across the state were without electricity, about 24,000 of them on Eyre Peninsula, and that the same wild weather later started to hit Adelaide, causing more than 3,000 properties to lose power because of suspected storm-related faults on the distribution network. Malinauskas said Thursday that eight hospitals across Eyre Peninsula and Ceduna on the West Coast had been affected and were operating on generators; InDaily, in its Friday report, quoted him as saying all of the hospitals' backup power systems had worked appropriately. AEMO Market Notice 146498, issued at 8:42 p.m. NEM time Thursday (8:12 p.m. ACDT Thursday, 3:42 a.m. CT) and reported by WattClarity, directed the Port Lincoln generating unit to synchronise and maintain local load and frequency control in an islanded system from 8:35 p.m. NEM time Thursday until further notice. Phone services on the peninsula were also reported to have been affected. ABC had also cited Telstra as saying there were currently total outages across 22 sites in the Eyre Peninsula, and the live blog said the blackout had also affected NBN services on the peninsula and, according to NBN, parts of the Northern Territory, including about 25 NBN sites and around 2,761 services in Ceduna, Cleve, Cowell, Port Lincoln, Wudinna, Kimba, Streaky Bay and surrounding communities; those telecommunications figures are not an electricity customer count.

outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. ABC News, in its Friday-afternoon article, quoted Premier Peter Malinauskas as saying at Friday's press conference that a bypass line was being installed to connect the West Coast and Upper Eyre Peninsula "later today." In an earlier Friday ABC live blog, Malinauskas said reconnection was "contingent on a few things," including the sustained operation of the generator in Port Lincoln, and that it "would see power restored to the upper Eyre Peninsula and West Coast later today, which would be a very good result given the significance and scale of the damage." That is not an official firm restoration time for all remaining customers. Temporary measures mentioned by Malinauskas also included crane installations to re-erect the transmission line and temporary tower installations in the coming days. The SA government had earlier warned it could take days to restore power in some areas. Malinauskas also said Friday that "we're not out of the woods yet," citing further storm events, extreme fire conditions over the weekend, and the risk that the aging Port Lincoln generator might fail. Power was restored to the Port Lincoln area using local generators at 9:45 p.m. ACDT Thursday, according to ElectraNet as reported by ABC News, but some properties remained without electricity as of 3:30 p.m. ACDT Friday, according to the SA Power Networks outage map as reported by ABC News.

outages.affected: UNE's Thursday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Thursday, Nov 19, with information attributed to UNE-MINEM, remains the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,780 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,050 MW available versus 2,800 MW of demand (a 1,750 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Thursday (5:00 a.m. CT), the grid had 1,050 MW available versus 2,180 MW of demand, leaving 1,132 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,250 MW affected at midday. On Wednesday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Wednesday affectation was 1,793 MW at 6:40 p.m. Wednesday. Wednesday solar photovoltaic output was 3,473 MWh, with a maximum of 540 MW at midday. The Thursday bulletin said unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. It said thermal generation limitations were 420 MW. Official UNE and Cubadebate sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. CiberCuba, in a Nov 19 daily summary citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, said that at 6:00 p.m. Cuba time Thursday (5:00 p.m. CT) the Havana utility reported 135 distribution circuits affected by a generation deficit and 309 MW affected in the capital. It said circuits with some of the longest affectation times included circuit 1247 in Playa, at 5 hours and 35 minutes, and circuits A223 and A219, at 4 hours and 41 minutes each, and that the utility also reported afternoon restorations on several circuits, including 1247, H443, A940, A490/S514, and A425. Those 135-circuit and 309 MW figures are official Havana figures from the capital utility as compiled by CiberCuba; they are not an official UNE national evening-peak actual and are not a customer count. outages.place: Johannesburg suburbs including Mayfair, Crosby, Brixton, Langlaagte, New Eldorado Park, Nancefield, Nirvana, Eikenhof, Pennyville, Industria, and Hursthill
outages.cause: City Power implemented an emergency isolation of the Fordsburg Substation on Thursday, Nov 19, after an incident at the Orlando Substation, interrupting supply to several substations in the south of Johannesburg. Earlier Thursday morning, City Power reported that lines one and two at the Fordsburg Substation had tripped. This is separate from the earlier Mayfair Substation fire and explosion that began Nov 8; City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena said Thursday morning that repairs at the Mayfair Substation following last week's fire and explosion have been completed
outages.affected: No official customer count from City Power for the Thursday outages. Jacaranda FM, in a Thursday, Nov 19 report updated at 5:03 p.m., said City Power confirmed it had to isolate the Fordsburg Substation after several substations were affected by an undisclosed emergency at the Orlando Substation. According to the utility, at least six substations in the south of Johannesburg were impacted by the emergency switch-off, including New Eldorado Park, Nancefield, Nirvana, Eikenhof, Pennyville, Industria, and Hursthill. City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena said technicians were deployed to the affected areas on Thursday morning, that technical teams and operators were on site investigating and assessing the emergency, and that the isolation was necessary to secure the network so assessments and interventions could be undertaken safely. Jacaranda FM said Rand Water, which supplies water to four municipalities, was among those affected, and that it was not yet known when technicians would restore power. EWN, in a Nov 19 report timed at 11:35, likewise said City Power had implemented an emergency isolation procedure at the Fordsburg Substation following an incident at the Orlando Substation, that the switch-off had interrupted supply to substations including Eikenhof, Industria, and Hursthill, that other affected areas included New Eldorado Park, Nancefield, Nirvana, and Pennyville, and that Mangena said an estimated time of restoration could not be provided because technical assessments were still under way. That isolation update is later than a 9:48 a.m. SAST Thursday SABC News report (1:48 a.m. CT), which said City Power reported another major electricity disruption after lines one and two at the Fordsburg Substation tripped, affecting several areas, including Mayfair, Crosby, Brixton, and Langlaagte. In that earlier report, Mangena said technical teams were on site investigating the cause of the fault and working to restore supply, and he clarified that the latest outage was at Fordsburg and not the Mayfair Substation, where repairs following last week's fire and explosion have been completed. Mangena said the latest disruption comes as the city continues to deal with more than 5,000 outage reports linked to storm damage, cable faults, theft, and vandalism; that is a citywide figure, not a customer count for the Fordsburg outage. Mangena's Thursday morning statement that Mayfair Substation repairs have been completed is later than Nov 18 newspaper reports about remaining Mayfair-area customers. Daily Maverick, in a Nov 18 article, and The Citizen, in a 5:40 a.m. SAST Wednesday, Nov 18 report (9:40 p.m. CT Tuesday), both said that while the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and some industrial areas in Crown Mines had had power restored, more than 20,000 residents of Mayfair, Crown Mines, Homestead, Vrededorp, Pageview, Jan Hofmeyr, and Amalgam would have to wait for at least another week before their power came back on. That more-than-20,000-residents figure was reported by those newspapers and was not attributed to a City Power official count. There is no national Eskom load shedding; this is a localized Johannesburg distribution outage. An evening Thursday recheck at 5:50 PM CT Thursday found no official City Power customer count for the Fordsburg isolation or the earlier Fordsburg trip, and no later official City Power restoration notice confirming that those Thursday outages had ended or that all remaining Mayfair-area cable-fault customers or Sentech had been restored. A late Thursday recheck at 11:55 PM CT Thursday, after Friday morning had begun in South Africa (about 7:55 a.m. SAST Friday, Nov 20), found no official City Power customer count for the Fordsburg isolation or the earlier Fordsburg trip, and no later official City Power restoration notice confirming that those Thursday outages had ended or that all remaining Mayfair-area cable-fault customers or Sentech had been restored.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found. A Thursday-morning recheck found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable. A midday Thursday recheck at 12:05 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable. An evening Thursday recheck at 5:50 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable. A late Thursday recheck at 11:55 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable.
